etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English inuren, equivalent to in- +‎ ure (“practise, exercise”).
senses: (transitive) To cause someone to become accustomed to something that requires prolonged or repeated tolerance of one or more unpleasantries. [from 16th c.]
(intransitive, chiefly law) To take effect, to be operative. [from 16th c.]
